Sniper Elite 5 is a case of one step forward, two steps back, and one of those steps backwards was straight into a pile of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. As I sit here scraping my boot, here are my main grievances:

1. Removal of Crouch Run: I have no idea who thought this was a good idea, it makes traversing open areas a case of squat walking at a frustratingly slow pace or full on running at normal height in full view of all and sundry, it makes moving stealthily into position much harder as you will frequently find that you are left accidentally standing at full height when attempting to make quick adjustments to your position . This is doubly baffling as to why it was removed as this was one feature Sniper Elite IV was praised for being "ahead of it's time".

2. White Outline when hiding inside bushes: Even playing on Authentic you still have a white line outlining your full body when you are concealed by a Bush... just why? it completely breaks the immersion and cannot be disabled from what I have seen so far, in Sniper Elite IV you knew you were concealed by vegetation when a sound played and your marker became fainter, was that not obvious enough or something?

3. Replacement of Infinite Stones with Finite Bottles: This is a particular bug-bare of mine as in previous Sniper Elite games you could cheese the entire games on any difficulty by luring away every German one at a time, this took hours though and was more a fault with the AI being too thick to realise that their battalion strength unit had mysteriously disappeared in the past couple of hours... This also completely ruins a secondary use for Stones, which was to destroy light sources, you can still do that with bottles... but for the fact that you only carry a base amount of FOUR. Meaning that if you want to destroy lighting to aid with your stealth you have to use bullets (great) instead or spend hours running back to pick up more bottles. This is like when they replaced Heat Sinks with Thermal Clips Between Mass Effect 1 & 2, it made no sense lore wise but was implemented to make the game less individual and more like every other third person cover shooter. 

4. Contrived map design & Invisible walls: This is quite possibly the worst area in which SE5 is a downgrade from SE4, despite having huge maps, instead of being large open sandbox typed areas everywhere instead seems like an extremely contrived series of arenas, invisible walls in the forms of low wall barriers, that for inexplicable reasons the player is unable to vault over, obvious cover and flanking points, like every area was purposefully designed for a Sniper's convenience. Sure SE4 did this somewhat too, yet the environments felt more like real world places, with more options open for the player to use their own initiative in completing objectives. Every map I have played so far just feels like a Sniper Elite 3 map on a larger scale. 

5. Invisible magnets: When enemies are alerted to you, by firing your gun or what not they will frequently fly into cover as if they are a big lump of metal being snapped into position by a large magnet. This also happens with the Player too when moving into cover and is perhaps one of the worse faults with this game as it can and will mess up your shots, picture this, you're in empty lung and are just waiting for an enemy soldier to run into your line of fire only for you to pull the trigger and the invisible hand of god to move them two meters to the left behind a wall in a fraction of a second. This will happen every time you try to kill more than one person in Empty Lung at a time. 

6. Everything has been Babyfied: Rebellion apparently worried that Easy was not Easy enough, and so have added a new Very Easy mode, and left out the Authentic Plus (future DLC?),  I couldn't tell you what the difference is, Authentic mode didn't seem all that much different from Very Easy, the Sniping even on Authentic seems to have had it's ballistics simplified to make hitting enemies easier. I was getting far more kills in Authentic in SE5 than I would do in SE4 playing without the Aim Assist.

7. Silenced Pistol pre-order bonus is only available for Axis snipers in Invasion mode. Self explanatory.

8. Hangovers from Multiplayer in Singleplayer: I don't know how universal this is, but I got really excited the first time I entered a Bunker on the first mission and saw a phone on the wall that said "Invasion only", my immediate thought was that if either I or the AI picked up that phone it would alert all of the Germans on the map to the Allied invasion of Normandy.. what a cool feature I thought, distracting all of the enemies from one side of the map whilst I sneak in the back. it took me a couple of seconds to realise that no, it's some multiplayer ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that has been left in the Singleplayer despite having "Invasion mode" disabled. If it's disabled it shouldn't be there, I've no idea what the stupid phone does and I'll never find out as the day I enable Invasion mode is the day I decide to swap my PC for a Mac. 

9. Lame Aesthetic: The Aesthetic of the previous games, the cute tutorial cards, the atmosphere, the UI, the HUD, the menus, it's all been stripped out, the game now looks like a generic multiplayer shooter with all of the little artistic qwerks and style sucked out of it giving a bland appearance.
 
10. To Rebellions in House BLM representation and equality adviser: Whilst there is no problem whatsoever with having Black playable characters in game, I find myself really really really having to stretch my imagination to believe that a Black SOE agent, a Black French Resistance Fighter and Black soldier of the Segregated 555th Airborne (a unit which never did active service in Western Europe, or anywhere outside the Continental United States for that matter during the war) have any place in a WW2 game set in North Western France during D-Day. It's less believable than the Nazi Super McGuffins that Rebellion comes up with every game, it breaks immersion though honestly the real issue with this is that it ignores the Racial Prejudices that were common amongst the Allied nations of the time and creates a false impression that people of colour were treated the same as Europeans, which they weren't by any European army/society of the time, indeed it trivialises the actual race struggles that took place. Don't get me wrong though the Axis side isn't portrayed any better, it portrays all of the Nazi's as being Germans when in actuality, many of those serving in North Western France during this time period were "Ost Regiments", that is Russians, Eastern Europeans, even Indians served in the SS on the Atlantic Wall. As the game is right now having any actual knowledge of history is a hindrance to enjoying the game.

I saw a lot of people complaining in pre-release reviews that this game was too similar to Sniper Elite 4, all I can say is that it's a shame that that is not true, If only they had made this a new campaign for SE4 it would have been brilliant, it's not though, it's Sniper Elite 3 with bigger maps, worse aesthetic an any game so far in the series and quite probably the weakest story yet. Bottom Line Upfront: This game has idiotic AI and hasn't meaningfully evolved since previous installments.

The only new mode to grace this title is the Axis Invasion, and this is by far the worst and most anti-thematic part of this game. Axis Invasion is a mode the developers added to punish players playing offline with less experience. The function of Axis invasion itself is atrocious. It allows random online players to constantly and continuously interrupt your single player experience with invasive mechanics that ruin the atmosphere of the game. It allows a fully equipped player character to run about the map unopposed, hunting you down with advanced intel on your location and activities. The developers demonstrated both a basic misunderstanding of sniper tactics and a refusal to let you play your way or give any advantages to you, the hero of the story, by punishing "camping" (aka basic sniping principles). This game mode essentially functions as a griefer shooting gallery that negatively impacts the experience in every possible way.

Beyond that, the campaign is not a meaningful experience in any way. The story is obtuse and unoriginal. All of the characters are angry and shallow, with no reason to care about them. But most damning, the AI is utterly worthless. In the event the enemy becomes alerted, which in inevitable unless you sneak around and refuse to snipe ANYONE, they immediately and idiotically charge you position, turning the game into a brainless duck hunt even on high difficulty. 

If endless unimaginative reiteration on x-ray testicle and headshots is worth $50 to you, then maybe you should get this game. If you are expecting any meaningful elaboration on the Sniper Elite formula, or just a game with rewarding or engrossing gameplay, avoid this game at all costs.

Honestly I just assumed this game would be kind of uninteresting and more or less just Sniper Elite 4 all over again, but I'm pleasantly surprised.

The most defining feature of Sniper Elite 5 is just how insanely big the maps are. Some of them are not only massive, but also incredibly detailed and impressive. I spent an entire 3 and a half hours on the first level alone. It's honestly surprising just how jam-packed full of content this game is.

The weapons are interesting. They chose a really weird selection of rifles, with 1 of the 6 not even being a rifle, one being an SOE prototype and one being a somewhat obscure French rifle. There´s an attachments system too that is actually fairly useful for optimizing different aspects of your guns. I made an M1 Carbine for myself, stripped it of all of its powerful features and slapped a suppressor on it to bring its audible range to about 30 meters. I´m sure it can probably go even lower if you play around with the attachments more.

It feels like the sniping is more realistic than before. In Sniper Elite 4, at about 100 meters you'd have to scope almost a full head length above somebody's head to hit them, but the large aim adjustments you're used to are much more subtle in Sniper Elite 5. You'll have to adjust for bullet drop and wind over long ranges, but to nowhere near as great an extent as in Sniper Elite 4. Overall, it feels more realistic and less arcadey.

For some reason the devs felt compelled to add a skill tree? I really don´t know why, as none of the skills are important and you´ll unlock them all in a few hours anyway. Were we meant to think hard about how we spend our skill points? Since you unlock everything so quickly, what´s the point of even thinking about it? Why does it matter if I unlock slightly higher lung capacity now or later? Why bother adding these faux RPG mechanics? My whole interaction with the skill tree was: "Oh, I forgot this existed. Whatever, let me just unlock this ♥♥♥♥ I guess." Why bother adding it? Or XP? Or a levelling system at all?

The story is once again just "evil Nazi general is making a device that will end the war yesterday, it's up to you to stop him!". I particularly loved how every single level had an objective where there's some kind of device that you can overload by pressing two buttons, then said device explodes and Karl goes "There, that'll slow down those Nazi bastards". And when I say every single level, that's surprisingly not even as hyperbolic as it sounds.

Lastly, the invasion gamemode is really interesting. You either invade someone who´s bleeding to death in a field surrounded by Germans on all sides and just blow his head off with ease or you invade someone who´s been dead quiet all game and have to wander the map looking for any sign of him, hoping that you find him before he finds you. It´s one of the most fun multiplayer stealth games I´ve played in a while.

For some reason though, there´s an anti-camping mechanic? In a game about sniping? If you sit in one spot for a few minutes, the game will mark you so the other player can find you. It makes sense in that it prevents the player from just hiding in a bush somewhere and being nigh impossible to find, but I hate that I take up a position overlooking somewhere I know the other player is going to go through, only for the game to ♥♥♥♥ me over and mark me for him to see. Surely I should be rewarded for having the patience and the basic deduction to recognize that if the player just completed an objective to my north and now needs to complete an objective to my south, they´ll have to pass through a certain place and that I can see said place from my position. But no, ♥♥♥♥ you, you´re camping, suck my ♥♥♥♥.

One last thing: Karl suffers from severe unable-to-shut-the-♥♥♥♥-up syndrome. I get it, people in real life think about things, they have an internal monologue, so it´s realistic for them to have an internal monologue in game too. Unfortunately, I don´t give a ♥♥♥♥ if long grass is good to hide in, or if the scopeless rifle I just picked up does not indeed have a scope. Karl loves to make useless observations and there´s really no need for it. You pick up an SMG and he´s like ¨Hmm, this SMG could do some damage...¨ Like, what? Grizzled war veteran picks up a gun and his first thought is ¨Hmm yes this gun can hurt people¨. After 100 hours in game I don´t need the main character to mumble that long grass is good to hide in or that a scopeless rifle is still useful.

All in all, there's nothing really wrong with it. The level design feels like a huge step up, the gameplay is more or less Sniper Elite 4's and the story is, again, less memorable than a conversation about washing machines.

Original Review: SE3 took the series away from being a stealth shooter to be more action based. SE4 expanded and improved upon that experience and provided an excellent blend of sniping and run-n-gun action with multiple ways to play a fairly open map.

SE5 is not that. It is a 3rd person action shooter with some sniper themes. Like an old 3rd person action shooter from the 2000s the levels are lane base and you don't have the freedom of movement of the previous two installments. On the subject of movement, Karl's movements just seem a little off. It's hard to describe but movement is both too fast and too slow while also being overly sensitive in some aspects. My biggest pet peeve is ladders and dropping down a ledge. Karl has a tendency to run past the ladder then dangle off the ledge before deciding to climb back up. He's very sensitive to understanding there is a ledge to hang off of, but not at all sensitive to the ladder he should be using to go up.

Dialogue in the Sniper Elite series has never been something to write home about, but this entry changes it. It really inspires you to get out your best fountain pen and practice your finest calligraphy to send a strongly worded letter over to Rebellion to tell them it sucks. It's like they tried to put effort into the story dialogue, but when you are making a B movie less is more. In this case, less certainly would have been more.

I'm going to skip over Invasion mode because I just turned it off. Not my cup of tea, thank you very much.

There are some things I very much like about SE5 though. Iron sights and kill cams for pistols and smgs. Also, enemies now only carry one long arm (if you remember in SE4 most of them were walking around with a sniper rifle and a smg), so at least the enemy has a reasonable weapons loadout compared to SE4. That's about it really.

As long as you are looking for a 3rd person action shooter where you get to run down your set lanes and kill everyone in your path, then you probably will be happy with SE5. But SE4 is just better and costs less. So why not just get SE4 and be on with your day?

The addition of the "Invasion" mode is inspired. having a player-controlled sniper loose on the map ratchets up the tension in a wonderful way, and the option to turn it off completely if desired is most welcome. I only hope that the player base keeps up enough to sustain quick matchmaking.

Let me first off say that I really enjoy playing this game with my buddy. We've played through almost all the SE games together, it's been fun and the set-piece being France is great, love the views and the works.

The odd climbing mechanics I can forgive, although it's sometimes confusing that I *can* run off of a random wall and just land, but if I want to run off of a beam in a stable, I have to meticulously hang off of the edge and drop down. Little honorable mention where we both managed to get ourselves stuck in the ground while trying to walk over a ramp (it made us hang off the edge of said ramp into the french dirt). 

These things are managable and probably patchable... BUT, I have some issues with the game as well. 

It feels like the game has been developed to have become more "Nazi shooting galary number 1944" (yes, I both mean that it's been done many times before AND that it's the year the game is set in. Thank you, observent reader). The customization is very interesting and I have taken much pleasure into creating (and finding) the most cursed guns on the face of this barren rock floating through space that we call Earth. Just for the reason of showing it off to my gun-nutting friends. 

That being said I feel like I don't need my rifle (as much) anymore since I can slap a scope on a welrod and proceed through the game with not too much of a fuss. And that's a slight issue. Not the customization but the fact that, dispite feeling like massive masochists and playing on the authentic difficulty, after a few missions we were casually walking up to our enemies, taking my sweet 3 seconds to aim at their nutsacks and preventing the birth of more of the nazi youth. I can casually walk through the streets of Mont Saint-Michel where the only annoyance was that sometimes we were invaded. That was the ONLY source of our challenges. And BOY do I have something to say about the invasions. 

I like the concept. You can be interupted mid-mission by an actually scarily good sniper and have an awesome face-off. Where-as the AI is... daft, you might find yourself being outplayed or simply jumped on by someone half a mile away who, wholeheartedly will give you a craniotomy. 

What you're apparently NOT allowed to do is, be a sniper. Maybe you dissagree but hear me out: You play a marksman, you are currently being hunted by a few dozen men and what do you do? I'd set up a few traps, find a nicely defensive possition with high ground and a bunch of windows to poke my barrel out of until I can make short work of my "hunters". What happened when I did this during a mission? 
I died, not because I was shot, not because I was stupid (which does happen sometimes, granted), not because of some sort of glitch or mishap... but because the game killed me for "camping". Let that sink in for 3 seconds. I am not allowed to stay in the same *building*. The game pinging me after a few minutes is annoying but I can accept it, it's not supposed to become a game of hide-and-seek, but it killed me because I refused to leave my carefully trapped church. Later in the game, when I didn't care anymore, I ran out towards the invader and I was still getting tagged, dispite active searching for the little ♥♥♥♥. And guess what? THEY found a defensive position with many an AI soldier to distract me with, hung out in-and-around a tower until I walked up to him. And did they get pinged? Nope. Did they get killed for not leaving their nicely defensive position? Nope. This is a load of bovine manure and I hope they change it. 

There's a last little mention I'd like to do about the special kill-list missions, which are hard to pull of sometimes because the AI just walks around and doesn't really go back to the area we're "supposed" to kill them, but that might just be us getting caught too many times. 

All-in-all, I like the game, I'm glad it's out but I'd only really recommend this if you have a friend to hang out with while doing so. Have a good day.

Edit: I'm reading in the update that they actually removed the part where you get kicked/killed for camping. Did not expect that.

Despite the popularity of the franchise, and the pedigree of the developer, Sniper Elite 5 is still very much an indie game. This isn’t any kind of secret, but it does set one’s expectations. From an indie game, one expects a certain level of jank. And oh boy, is this game janky.
Not in the sense of being necessarily buggy - I’ve personally only encountered one game-breaker bug at time of writing - but more in the sense of design flaws. Despite being able to climb vines and lattices like Spider-Man, old Karl can never seem to clamber up a waist-high ledge, or navigate any of the many tiny fences and hedges that constitute the game environment’s unnecessarily plentiful invisible walls. He will also often just get stuck on things, like bits of rubble or slightly irregular terrain. And why is the cover system not governed by a button-press? Why does Karl have to rub up against the brickwork and hope for the best?
There are numerous other, petty ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ I could list - such as no longer being able to throw infinite rocks, but having to rely on limited bottles - but won’t because you already aren’t going to read all this.
This is Sniper Elite *5*, I remind you. Rebellion has had 5 games to buff this franchise to a mirror shine, and yet… This remains a game of contrast, and weirdness. Character models are beautiful and high-fidelity, but animate like theme-park mascots. The series’s trademark X-Ray kills look better than ever, but there’s very little actual gore - in that damage is almost never actually shown on enemies. No dismemberment, even if they were hit in the teeth with a Panzerfaust. Little if any blood, even through they were just stabbed directly in the neck.
These may seem like small details, because they are. But their absence detracts from the overall experience.
And speaking of that overall experience… Yeah it’s still great. There are few things in gaming as satisfying as watching a bullet tunnel through the childhood memories of some Nazi scumbag. Sniper Elite 5 isn’t a bad game by any stretch of the imagination, but it is underwhelming. Myself, and many others, were just expecting more. I recommend it, but maybe wait for a sale if you’re on the fence.

You can see it, but you cant shoot or get close to it, due to invisible wall, called hedge.

That comes to third part, invasions. If you are invader, you feel practically god. It is so badly balanced, that you want to cry for the person you invaded. Warning! Do NOT buy this game if you want a "Sniper game" experience. SE5 is a sniper game that most of the time does not want you to snipe anything but rather to handle things with short ranged weapons and melee. 

But let us begin from the start: After SE4 and its fantastic maps you would think that Rebellion would have figured out the formula and just build and improve on it. Well, SE5 is a testimony that they clearly did not understand what made SE4 such a success and decided to make a step back in several directions. 

Map design: probably the greatest flaw. While in SE4 you had vast, open sandbox maps, SE5 right from the start brings a map that seems open at first glance, but is cut in pieces and tunnel-like parts by untraversable hedges. Ah, yes, who does not know, France, land of the steel hedges, that can never be traversed. Remember the bushed on SE4 where you could hide? Gone. No bush can be entered, together with trees they form fixed barriers to guide the player where he has to go. It almost feels like level design from the early 2000s. Some of the later maps open up quite a bit, but more than often, map design is such convoluted that only close combat quarters is possible. You can expect that ocassionally, but all the time!? Out of the 8 main maps I would say maybe 3 offer some good sniping experience, for the others I (and also several members in the forums) found it much more effective to go in guns blazing with SMG and grenades or just melee. Is that the experience the developers wanted the players to have? 

Graphics: they are ok, but not on par you would expect from a game that came out in 2022. Faces seem wooden, but at least the animations are very fluid and nice to look at. Map optics gave me more than often a sense of depression. While in SE4 you really felt like on vacation in Italy, with just some sniping to do and having a glass of wine in a wonderful scenery afterwards, well, in most of these maps I cannot wait to get away from them. Yes, in some way they capture the essence of what it might feel to be in France, but it is presented in such a horrid way, the feeling of life that the SE4 maps had is lost here almost completely. 

X-ray and gore: I do not put a lot of weight on this one, but objects vanishing in thin air during the x-ray just feels strange. Also, while during x-ray your bullets seem to inflict a lot of damages, this in no way is displayed on the corpse afterwards. It just feels inconsistens, and there is no improvement (I could notice) over SE4. 

Controls: It has been some time since I played SE4, but I do not recall it to be that whacky. I have problems going through doors, it just does not feel accurate. Climbing down ladders is horrid, why not complete a sliding option like most normal games have? Apart from that, the sniping mechanic is excellent, at least that!

Bugs and flaws: Sometimes laughable, sometimes just sad. I wanted to melee an enemy at a control post, just to find out he was places 1m away behind the level boundary. So while he was enjoying shooting at me, I stood there like an idiot, 1m away, not able to reach him. Items are frequently placed where you cannot reach them (the pickup key just does not show), enemies sometimes float around - it gives an impression of a game not properly tested at all. 

Enemy AI: ha, you will be pleasently surprisded - not! They are either dumb as **** and run directly into your kill zone with 20 of their dead soldiers already laying on the floor, or they are absolute killing beasts, spotting you through fields of flowers and obsacles from hundred meters away and more just to open fire with their short ranged weapons to hit you with pin-point accuracy. Karl could learn a lot from them. 

What Rebellion took away: You would expect that with the excellent experience SE4 was the devs would understand what made the game successful. No, they did not. Instead, for no reason anybody in the forums could understand, they take away certain mines and wire traps in order "not to confuse the player". Aha, yes, got it. Those items were essential on higher difficulties in SE4, and now they are gone. They are implemented in the game, in multiplayer, so why take them away from SP? Also, weapon choice even with everything unlocked right now is quite... disappointing. I guess they reserved the good ones for later DLCs etc.

Story? Never did matter, and also does not here. Rebellion, if you want to cut costs, just cut those horrible cringy cut-scenes and dialogues, because really no one gives a ****. 

All in all: after getting all previous SE games on a 80% discount (I arrived late to the party) and having so much fun I wanted to give something back and preordered this one. Why? What the hell have you been doing for the last half decade??

If I had anything nice to say, it would be on the improved graphics, the lush scenery, the attention to detail of the buildings and their decor, the dev team's creativity on the cool looking wall posters (thumbs up to Ricardo and co), but that's about it. As for the actual gameplay and gamer/user experience, it's like the Face Off movie but for video games.... same body, different look. The maps control where you can and can't go which is just stupid! What ever happened to the open world style that you gave us in SE4? Also, I can climb a wall like a superhero, but I can't step over a 2-foot fence? The AI is almost laughable too. On easier modes, you secretly kill one guard and the rest follow one by one to the exact same spot which takes out any sort of challenge at all. On some of the harder modes, if you happen to get spotted, well, you realise that you cannot hide anywhere because it is almost as if the game tells the AI where you are located.... all the time (even if you run away and hide)..... and the experience turns into an all out shoot-em-up just to avoid being chased (so much for trying to be stealthy and hiding and stuff). 

The game is a bit clunky/buggy too as I often find myself trying to almost step over a table in order for the game to recognise that I am trying to pick up a gun/bottle/important papers etc. And what happened to the Playstation button config? I am using a PS5 controller on PC through Steam and all I see is Xbox button configs during game play. My same gaming set up works fine with Sniper Elite 4 showing PS buttons, but now with Sniper Elite 5, they only show Xbox buttons (why would you do this to your PS on PC gaming fans??). 

The levels are longer and that's great! Unless you are a professional historian who will appreciate the different array of available old guns (which all sound exactly the same, I might add), the game is simply a longer barrage of SE4 but without the sniping ability (because like, AI sort of know where you are now and so you pretty much have to turn into Rambo of some sort and shoot your way out). 

So, for players who are looking for that kind of experience, they'll probably be ok with paying the AU$70 for this. But, for the avid SE fan who has enjoyed your series since the beginning and looking for something new and exciting, will most likely be disappointed (like myself) in the overall game play and user experience, wondering what the hell Rebellion was thinking when they put this into production.

The first game in this series came what? 13 years ago? From playing this, you would never suspect this was the fifth game in a series that is more than a decade old now. The level of polish and general "jank" is high and more in line with something you would see from an amateur team's first effort at this type of game. At this point, there is an obvious lack of effort and the dev seems content just churning out the same game over and over (even the first DLC is identical to the last time). Here is a non-exhaustive list of issues. I cannot emphasize enough that some of these occurred in the previous games as well.

- Permanently stuck in a looting animation, reloading does not help (had to restart from a different save).
- Stuck in pistol reloading animation. Pistol keeps automatically reloading and puts zero rounds in the mag, even though I have plenty of ammo in reserve.
- Multiple times stuck in/on environmental obstacles and invisible walls. This is especially grating when you try to melee someone and get stuck in geometry such as a non-pathable bush, alarm tripod, etc.
- Melee kill animations that will not trigger, especially when guards are trying to raise an unconscious guard. One time this outright disabled melee kills for long enough to get mowed down.
- The automatic cover system "locks" you to nearby objects, but you can't lean against many objects that look like you should be able to. Worse, there are environmental elements like low walls that conceal your character but are not actually "cover" and thus enemies can see you over them (even though the object is blocking their view).
- Grabbing enemies as they come around a corner is wildly inconsistent. Sometimes you can trigger the kill animation, most times your character disconnects from the cover and can't do it. There's a "sweet spot" where it triggers, but it's where your head and half your torso is sticking out so you look like an idiot.
- If you do get a corner grab, often you toss the body into the geometry and the ragdoll spazzes out and gets stuck in furniture or glitches through the world. Inexplicably, sometimes this damages you?
- Multiple times when a bolt cutter animation would not trigger, or character would simply sit still for a few seconds before activating.
- Enemies that randomly go into "suspicious" state for unknown reasons on far corners of the map. In some cases I played entire missions with the enemy in "hunting" state even though I am long gone.
- Telepathically linked Jaeger enemies. I take out an isolated soldier quietly and out of sight, suddenly his entire squad is alerted and knows the exact pinpoint location where he was knocked out and runs over.
- Enemies that surround you in bushes and then just stand there... alerted.. looking at you.. doing nothing... sometimes a guy runs in and you stab him in front of his friends.
- Enemies that look directly at you and do.. nothing.. sometimes they don't even alert they just stare directly at you.

And a special mention:

- I fired a "non-lethal" round that punched straight through a guy's skull. After the X-ray "killcam" he was tagged "unconscious". I can't harsh the game too much for this though because it was hilarious. I kept shooting regular bullets that counted as non-lethal because the game glitched ammo switching.

The high point are the levels, they look nice and are mostly fun to play. There are enough paths and detailed areas littered throughout that they feel bigger than they are except for the occasional invisible wall (really? In 2022?). The rest of the features on the Steam page are embarrassingly shallow though. There are only a handful of weapons that come with the game, I am sure that gets better if you buy the already announced six (!) weapon DLCs. The customization is mediocre - there are maybe one or two decent builds for each gun, the only real game-changer is the suppressor, everything else is minor stat changes. Visual skins for guns are limited (only two each, same for all guns I think) and character customization lets you only pick a character and their hat, I am sure that gets better if you buy the already announced two character packs.

I bought 3, 4, and now 5 and this is the last one I will be buying. In the interest of constructive criticism, maybe it would be better to spend more time polishing the game and making a higher quality product than finding clever ways to monetize content that should have been in the base game?

# My review of Sniper Elite 5

I have just complete Sniper Elite 5 after just 18.5 hours and feel let down. In fact I will need to replay Sniper Elite 4 again to help regain my respect for the series.

## Mileage might vary

These are my own personal opinion as a paying customer (having bought SN3, SN4 and SN5).

## The Good
- visually more rich, lush maps and breathtaking views
- The toggle aim mode is nice idea but not that useful
- Large, open landscape feels more open world (but is not)


## The Pointless
- zip-lines (What? Wait. You are an elite sniper, but you want to broadcoast to the entire army you are crossing a field?)
- bolt cutters (you are carrying rifles, pistols, grenades etc.. but cannot smash a padlock or pick it. Why!)
- bolt cutters (you have to hunt around and find them)
- The invisible "Mission boundaries" (ugly, terrible and lazy design. Why not drop a truck, fallen tree or crater in road instead of the glass wall?) I've been killed a few times due to glass walls.
- While already searching enemy the voice over "Something tells me this guy is worth searching..." (why not say this before the search?)
- buildings and rooms are filled with many, many objects (but none can be interacted with and only help hide which items you can actually interact with)
- Boring maps (after a few handfuls of nazis you will find the huge factories and levels totally empty)
- Animations seem to block player controls (even some built-in 0.5 second delay before performing actions)

## The Bad
- Grenade throwing bug (auto switch to grendes after applying last med pack - WHY!)
- The 222 armoured car disappears, but you still need to destroy it by bridge (unable to complete misson, had to restart it)
- Picking up items (often you need to stand up and look down to interact with an item)
- Opening crates (Stand near end of a crate and you will see the [E] open option but you cannot perform action)
- Moving up/down steps (really, really bad animation which looks like a gym workout video capture. It does NOT fit with walking/running animation)
- Game exit hangs with 'Sniper5_D3D12_Retail_Submission" is not responding (need to hit [CTRL] [SHIFT] [ESC] to kill task)
- Enemy takedown when laying on ground (the enemy will stand up to play the animation)
- Enemies will appear to die and then jump back up and fight without any damage
- The silent pistol are lousy. There are times you need to fire 6 hits (even to the head) to kill an enemy
- Even at close range you need to use an entire clip of ammo (the sten gun is garbage)
- The action 'E' key sometimes fails and you need to re-aim looking down to trigger the action.
- The hit zones on enemies are suspect (the same aim on SN4 kills in a single hit in SN5 you could need 5!!)

## Future of Sniper Elite (I hope!!!)
The game has always yelled out for needing to be a truly FPS (first person shooter) and there are strong indications of that in SE5. The really annoying switch between first and third person loses your aim. When going up steps you encounter the 'I thought I would be able to shoot from here, but can only see the top step!' issue.

Just ADD A FIRST-PERSON MODE for SN6. I really hate the tomb raider style camera mode and having to re-aim/focus on the target.

## Summary
I'm a big fan of the Sniper Elite series. The fourth installment remains the best so far. The SE5 looks good, but feel empty in places with lack of opponent snipers or waves of Nazis to challenge you. I remember Sniper Elite 1 and the sniper-vs-sniper gameplay, fighting tanks and stalking your enemy. 

Sniper Elite 5 feels like an abandoned theme park (looks good but no atmosphere)

As a player with over 1,700 hours in SE4 and completed SEV2 and SE3, I feel pretty letdown so far. I only play on Authentic. I REALLY want to like this game. But after playing a few more hours, it appears that Rebellion has jumped the shark with this release.

1. There is no wind on the majority of the game I have played, eliminating the challenge of compensating for that. You would have figured they could have at least put in some significant winds when you are on the coastline literally staring at the English Channel. The shooting mechanics have now become unskilled center of crosshair shooting. The wind feels so non-existent from my gameplay that I've been actually questioning if it's a bug. Yes, I get that it was exaggerated in SE4 / SE3 / SEV2, but that made it fun and differentiated the rifles and muzzle velocities, and gave an additional acquired skill factor. You no longer really have to zero a rifle, because it doesn't matter. I don't even look at the wind indicator anymore because it doesn't move 98% of the time. It doesn't feel like a sniping game anymore.
2. The bullet trails coming off enemies bullets look like jumbo jet contrails. I would have thought they could be toned down or removed in Authentic.
3. As others have mentioned, I do not know why they went in the misguided direction of all the non-lethal stuff.
4. I liked the movement of SE4 better. SE5 feels clumsier, almost reminiscent of the clumsiness that SE3 felt like.
5. The coop survival mode camaraderie of reviving people now takes a turn for the worse due to needing medkits to revive your teammates. So all you can do is watch them go down and die if you don't have any to spare. And of course if you use them on a teammate, you no longer have them to heal yourself.
6. In coop survival, ammo at command posts can now be challenging to share. One person can walk up to the command post after a wave has started and basically take it all, leaving no ammo for teammates. That is going to case a lot of tension, and also be a camaraderie breaker.
7. The white outline around your character while your character is in foliage in Authentic is tacky looking and really takes away from the experience of actually feeling like you are hidden in a bush.
8. When you are playing survival, even in Authentic, they put white outlines around the last 5 guys. Seriously, training wheel kid ♥♥♥♥ like that shouldn't be in Authentic.
9. There aren't many snipers in coop survival, and it looks like the positions of them aren't going to vary much. They also seem to be less of a threat than the snipers on SE4.
10. The AI is completely brain-dead. Often, you'll find guys just sitting there inexplicably while a complete gunfight is going on. Their reaction time is slow, and you can just run at them and melee then before they even think about shooting at you.

Hopefully things like these get adjusted in patches, SE5 has been two or three steps back from what they had going in SE4. It's hard to determine if they are trying to only appeal to the casual gamer that just wants to run through the game like it's a movie and dumbed down the skill level to remedial levels for them.

Rebellion dumbed down the difficulty of SE5 bigtime by pretty much removing bullet wind mechanics, and making the AI clueless in comparison to previous SE games. So unless they address major things like that, the game might indeed just be plain boring. It's so far off from being fun in the skill regard that I don't even know if they'll be able to salvage it with patches. Most of the die hard regular SE4 players that I know feel that way. And that comes from someone who has played over 1700 hours of SE4 and REALLY wanted to love SE5.

[b]Gameplay/Gunplay: 90/100[/b]
Recommend playing Authentic difficulty because the other options just make it feel like an Ubisoft handhold-trip with X-ray markings, hud indicators out the wazzo. Added mechanics of Non-Lethal allows for (mostly) pacificst runs and easier setups on the complicated "kill X with Y weapon or Z item" by allowing you to move the body before ending the digital heartbeat. Also Coop with friendly fire on is great fun. 

Invasion is a wonderfully fun time, a good game of Cat-and-Mouse, but the problem is most people don't really know how to actually play the game like a sniper and just run around like its a run-n-gun shooter, so they usually ragequit instead of hunting, and it leads to idiots who don't read the instructions complaining about what an "annoying feature it is" and not turning it off for some reason or how having it disabled "reduces the XP gain". XP gain really is not an issue in this game. Since unlocks are tied to in-level objectives, and Multiplayer and Singleplayer are separate XP trees completely, it does not matter.

Coop and Cross platform function work great, although they should make it clear to players that engaging in a sniper duel Mouse vs Controller is NOT recommended for most people.

[b][/b]Story: Who cares its a damn sniping game. Works well, didn't question the settings or locations.

[b]Sound Design:[/b]
Guns sound fantastic, as does the masking SFX and localized voice positioning. The headshot SFX is satisfying. Footsteps are muddled, and the low-health state where everything echos and they add a white balance filter should be removed. Don't think it should be replaced with jelly or anything, just remove the low-hp UI state as its incredibly annoying. As usual, I play with music off in multiplayer modes, and since I play with invasion on that means I have music completely off.

[b]Critiques:[/b]
I see people complaining about confusion on "climbing, vaulting" etc. Some of it is 100% valid. Some environmental and level designs are done for a reason, but the coverup and justification to the player is presented as a 2m tall bush that they cant jump over sometimes. Personally I never had an issue, might because I played the previous games and am familiar with the level design style already. The problem is the game LOOKS like a modern open-world style level design, but it is still DESIGNED in a somewhat linear nature. People might just assume they can go anywhere and do anything based on how it looks.

Invasions: 
This could be the perfect defining addition to sniper elite, however it does need some tweaks, as it is INCREDIBLY skewed towards the invader. In addion, the spawns need to be reworked as I sometimes spawn DIRECTLY FACING the enemy player, meaning I have an easy kill.  The designs should make it hard for the INVADER, not the other way around.

By default, Invasions should be turned off and players should have to make a choice and effort to enable them. Most people are casual players and due to the incredibly unbalanced design for the Invader, will easily get hunted with no actual cat-mouse fight occuring. Its also incredibly enligtening to see just how bad some people are, not even hunting them just watching them fight NPCs and realzing that they literally have zero chance against an invader even on a 2-v-1 and probably just skipped through all the prompts about invasions.

When an enemy invades, the host player should KNOW the area the sniper deployed in and not have to mess around with the stop-gap mechanic of "invasion phones". It really feels like they couldn't figure out a way to inform invaders of host activity without just TELLING them the position. All the NPC invasion spot mechanics should be the only thing needed for a hunter to narrow down the location of their prey. Also, being able to invade people on their FIRST TIME THROUGH a level really is not that fair. Invasions should be an optional thing that can be enabled for re-visits of a campaign level, not as the first experience.

Horde mode and Multiplayer are fine, could just a bit of adjustment for each but honestly co-op and invasions are why I got the game. 


As for the whole "waaahh you are humanizing nazis by allowing non-lethals" childrens section. Its a video game. Who cares? You being bothered by it says more about you than it does about the developers adding in a new playstyle method. Its an OPTION, don't wanna use it, don't have to use it, never ever had to use it unless you are going for the 100% achievements, and even after you pacify the enemies, you can still kill them to sate your digital bloodlust.

So I was not going to post a review but then saw the negative ones and decided to add my comments. This game is great. I am in my 60's and have a case of the shakes in my right hand from sniffing too much white glue, I guess ;-). So I play at the Cadet level. The game is smooth as butter, the graphics are crisp and I playing with a CPU which is 5 generations back from the minimum requirements, though my GPU is a bit more modern, it is an RTX 2060 (which means the CPU bottlenecks the GPU by up to 40% at times). But, at 2k the game plays without any lag. 

Someone put in a negative review because the verticality was not like Assassins Creed. Yeah, go figure, 2 different types of games. One based on a sniper in WWII and the other based on complete fantasy with a hero who is a parkour specialist. Big wonder. Sniper Elite was never much on vertical movement. This one is a shade more vertical than the last. I like the shade of difference. There are obstacles to movement. They add to the fun because you have to find a way of dealing with them as you move around to sneak to the enemy. 

Mission 1 is pretty much structured as a tutorial, so it does seem a lot less open than previous incarnations of the game. But believe me, it gets very, very open world in missions after that one. 

There are improvements on the game. This is about the first game I have encountered that treats suppressors like they are in the real world. If you have ever heard the noise a suppressed gun makes in the real world, you will appreciate this game because when you fire one, there better be no enemies close by or there better be some sort of noise in the background doing what they call a sound mask. Mind you, I am still just at mission 3 and the suppressors might be more sound defeating later on. Hollywood and 99% of games get it wrong all of the time. Firing a gun with a suppressor on it does not sound like a mouse just farted. It makes less noise than an unsuppressed weapon but it still makes quite a bit of noise.

As the invasion part? Well I never like multiplayer as I generally cannot stand people so no big issues with it on my side. I just play without it. Who cares if I get less XP than someone who plays with it? I am never going to play against anyone in the game. I do not give a rat's hind end about who got what XP doing what mission and how long it took them. 

There are some design choices that I question, or they are bugs. I am at mission 3 and yet the game has not saw fit to give me the choice of additional rifles to choose from. SMG and pistols? Yeah, I have choices. Rifles? No! Sure you can pick up discarded weapons but you can never reload them. So if they have 7 or 8 bullets in them, that is all you will get to fire and then you will have to discard it. I was led to expect that if you brought a discarded weapon to one of the gun benches, you could then configure it into your choice of loadouts. Nope, you cannot!  Whether this is a bug or intentional, I am getting quite tired of my 2 beginning rifles by this time. If i cannot get an additional rifle without getting a DLC, then I will be very annoyed.

Finally the sound mask thing where you sabotage a vehicle or generator to get a sound mask? Well there is a bug there or poor design choice. If there are any enemy within hearing range of said device, you better wipe them all out because they will forever go into investigative mode and show up as huge orange question marks in the UI and in the game itself. It is VERY annoying. By mission 3, I was no longer sabotaging anything. You might say, well the solution to that is to wipe out all enemies. Yeah well, in mission 3 there is a generator you can sabotage right at the start of the mission. Then a dozen enemies well within the mission map all go into investigative mode. And by the time you have ferreted them all out, you have had it with the INVESTIGATIVE mode and the whole sabotage/sound mask mechanic. If it is a bug, it should be fixed. But if it is a design choice, go back to the old way of creating sound masks please because the new way is just plain annoying.

Oh and I thought Rebellion had stated to have fixed the bug where enemy could shoot you when they were out of sight around a corner??? Well it has not been fixed. Mind you they do it a bit less now, but they can still do it. Annoying. 

Overall, though, I give them 4 stars out of 5,

TLDR: This is a step back from Sniper elite 4, and shows severe signs of being rushed after SE VR's failure. Gone now is the fun sandbox design of sniper elite 4 with huge massive maps that may contain outposts that exist solely to be eye candy and world building, or target practice, instead we now have dark souls invasions. Metal gear solid 2 Non lethal ammo, with the same fatal flaw as metal gear solid 2. And XP nerfs that encourage charging in with a maxed out SMG and rifle with non lethal ammo to get that sweet chunk of XP you used to get for farting in time with an ambient sound. 

The long versions: 

Map design: The maps are HUGE, EASILY some of the biggest of the series that aren't called "San Celini Island" and "Aquaduct". But the problem lies in the fact that every map is so JAM packed with side objectives that if you see a Nazi walking around somewhere you can bet your ass there is an objective there. Alternate paths have been SEVERELY limited based on this fact, likely due to the dark souls invasion mechanic which can be opted out of, (more on that later). 

  You get about 2 alternate paths to each objective which consists of climbing walls that are poorly indicated by white objects such as dead vines, smears of white paint, or French resistance graffiti tags that the Nazis don't seem to give a ♥♥♥♥ are plastered all over the place, or you can just run across the fields and you MIGHT find some broken fence somewhere you can crawl under or a waist high fence that CAN be vaulted over, as opposed to the 30 feet of the exact same fence beside it that you CAN'T vault over. 

Weapon selection (Warning: gun collectors and sniper elite veteran's rant ahead): Remember the Mosin? The gun in almost every sniper elite game since the first game? Rebellion doesn't, or more accurately cut it to package it into a DLC (this was written prior to the DLC all being released If I'm wrong, I'm wrong, but I am willing to bet steam points I'm not). You have a narrow selection of about 4 weapons per category suited to the french theater, kinda. Instead of things like the liberator or M3 grease gun that were air dropped for french resistance fighters prior to Operation overlord (D-day for the non historically inclined) You have an american selection, a German selection, a couple british guns, and a French RSC from 1918. A gun that barely saw production and was, had WWI not been declared, planned to be the first ever Semi-auto rifle. The m1 Garand from sniper elite 3 (and 4's DLC), the king of ping, has been replaced by the M1a1 Carbine. 
    
  The Thompson is obscenely powerful when maxed out and I often found myself, instead of sniping, running around like an idiot with a rapid fire Thompson with a suppressor and a 100 round drum cutting down entire patrols before they can raise an alarm like scenes out of a gangster movie instead of a WWII sniper game (more on why later). 
    
  The 1911a1 also makes a return and honestly, except the welrod from the prior games and the Mark 6 Webley revolver, the pistols all feel no different from each other, so I'm not going to go too in-depth on them, the first example I've cited of a rushed game. 

  The German list isn't really worth going into too much detail in. A Kar98, a G43, a walther P.08 an STG44, and an MP40 that I can think of off the top of my head. All fairly unremarkable and standard for the series at this point. 

  Silencers are more accurate to reality, they are SUPPRESSORS, not SILENCERS. Hollywood silence is only achieveable using ammo that doesn't break the sound barrier, IN conjunction with a suppressor. And even then only on certain calibers. For example the .22 long rifle. Suppressing an m1911 and still using supersonic ammunition still results in the sound being about as loud as a lawnmower.

  Honestly I could, and SHOULD go on, but I'm not getting paid for this and I have limited space that I have somehow managed to hit. 

Weapon unlocks: THANK GOD THE WEAPON CHALLENGES ARE GONE! Oh God, now you have to unlock weapons by beating missions, you can't just pick them up anymore due to how small the weapon pool is. And here we have the second example of a rushed game -- arbitrary limitations that were lifted in the prior game in the series (not including SE VR). The kar98, which is POSSIBLY one of the better guns in the game tied with previous installments variants of the mosin, isn't unlocked until almost the final mission -- assuming you even get the record for completing it which I'll cover later in bugs. 

  In order to unlock upgrades for the weapons you have to go on an easter egg hunt for the weapon workbenches in each level, I'm not sure how to feel about this as I like the idea of having to scavenge the equipment and not having SOE resupply you like in SE4, and it gives incentives to find intel documents and officers with the keys to FIND said workbenches. This illusion however, is then destroyed by you walking within 20 feet of the workbenches location, and it being marked on the map. Then you can either find the key or, since half the map is likely aimbotting your location at that point anyway unless you are carrying non lethal ammo with a silenced weapon, just throw a satchel charge on it and go in. I have mixed feelings on this. But I DO lean towards it being a pro since I had to farm liver shots to max out the mosin in SE4. And the horrid "high heart rate challenge" massacres that consisted of setting the game to cadet, sprinting everywhere and emptying a mag into people's heads.

Story: Let's face it, we are all here to shoot Hitler in the balls, listen to Karl crack one liners (Which he doesn't do very often in this game) and kill Nazis. It's a standard sniper elite story. Nazi has secret project, Karl finds info on it, you go to win the war single-handedly. Moving on.

Bugs: Todd Howard called. The rental of bethesda's QA team is up.
  Where do I START? You go to open a door, hit whatever button you have bound to interact, and Karl stands there admiring the French architecture for about 30 seconds before he opens it. In the meantime some Jerry from the other side of the map has spotted you because apparently EVERY German in 1944 decided that carrots were their ONLY food, called reinforcements from Fallschirmjäger, and now the entire base is emptying bullets into your dome. You get into the door with ONE bar of health, maybe less, pull out your trusty WAY OVERPOWERED maxed out thompson, and it seems Karl has retained EVERY SINGLE EMPTY MAGAZINE EVER AND WILL RELOAD INFINITELY UNTIL YOU CHANGE AMMO TYPES. You change ammo types, Nail the active reload taken from gears of war (A nice addition, by the way) to reload faster, go to a wall that you climbed up before and hurl yourself over the side to escape the swarms of fire coming your way, And because you have to hold space to vault, Karl immediately pulls himself BACK up the ledge, and dies. You reload, fix the reload bug, and just decide to execute everyone before they become a problem, then proceed to admire the door for 30 seconds again. Remember how I said I often ended up just gunning down entire squads with the Thompson? Yeah this is why. I'm sure -- Actually I'm HOPEFUL these bugs will get fixed. Especially the infinite reload as it means that if you get this bug on ANY gun and you are OUT of alternate ammo, the gun is now broken entirely. I've had pistols do it, I've had rifles do it, I usually end up seeing it on the SMG's because they end up being my most used weapon. 
  
I don't know if the AI's eagle eyes are a bug or intentional so I'm putting it here, because ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ these guys can spot you at a range and hit you with irons that would make Simo Häyhä, Francis Pegahmagabow, and Carlos Hathcock, jealous. Forget the war, Hitler should have invested in a trick shooting team to push his ideology.

In summary:
  Since I'm at the character limit: wait for a sale. Use non lethal at all times you can because it gives more XP.

Sniper Elite 5 plays really well on my PC.  The scenery is beautiful and the game feels more fluid.  I prefer single-player campaign and have no opinion on the invasion or the multiplayer mode.  Having played this for 4+ hours at the first review time and 24+ hours for the second review, I have overall enjoyed the game's smoothness, graphics, and I like the improvements over the previous installments.  The game feels even more modern, but still retains the original Sniper Elite characteristics, such as x-ray cameras, bullet ballistics, difficulty levels, and traditional stealth or loud options with multiple ways to progress through each mission, which makes this an all too familiar game and genre.  I have not encountered any crashes, frame rate issues, or errors.

Pros:
- Beautiful scenery and graphics
- Massive levels with multiple approach and tactics
- Different ammo types
- Rifle iron sights and first person view for all weapons
- X-ray camera for all weapons

Cons:
- No crouch-and-run mode (this was a great ability in SE 4)
- No Shooting Range to practice with weapons and earn medals
- Too many invisible walls and inaccessible terrain
- No customization for Karl (no different outfits, jackets, etc., which was great in SE 4)
- No AP or tripwire mines
- Limited distraction objects (SE 4 had unlimited rocks, while SE 5 has limited bottles)

Neutral:
- Silenced weapons are not truly silent, but this keeps the game interesting.
- There is not enough weapons to choose from, and weapon modifications do not make up for this.  SE 4 had more rifles, pistols, and SMG's to select from.

Thank you, Rebellion, for delivering such a great game, but some improvements are definitely worth including in SE 5, especially the crouch-and-run option for stealthy approach.  Perhaps, these will arrive in the future updates or DLCs.

My thoughts after 90 hours or so:

The Good:
Distances have greatly improved over SE 4 and so have the bullet physics, no longer do you need to zero a normal rifle for 50m to hit someone, meaning you get to shoot at longer distances now, although it is still very much dependent on the map design for performance reasons.

Gear overall has seen an upgrade. with pistol and smgs being capable of holding their own, combined with the gun customization you can actually make quite diverse loadouts (especially if you got the dlc). A big bonus is that the customisations also work on authentic which wasn't a thing prior, basically completely removing that element of the game on higher difficulties. I think the devs found a good middle ground where optical zoom and silencer capability is limited on authentic now (still makes the game incredibly easy on anything below that imo)

The new secondary objectives, kill list and workshops incentivise exploration and I enjoy them.

Maps are varied and overall fun.

The new invasion mode is a good addition overall and I hope for it to return with some tweaks.

The Questionable:
Some of the weapon upgrades and cosmetics are very jank and questionable, we got magazines inserted the wrong way, rifle silencers on pistols, extended mags for welrods and blue electrical tape as grip tape that lets you aim better.

The maps are riddled with invisible walls making traversal intuitive and frustrating sometimes.

The addition of "non lethal" ammo and mines (?!?) for every gun was not needed and it leaves a bad taste in my mouth that we now have non lethal weapons in a game about killing Nazis. Furthermore the game doesn't do anything with it, you can't interrogate them, there is no optional mission to kidnap an officer or something. It just is in there because modern stealth games need to have this cause of MGS.

The Bad:
Authentic Plus is gone. The highest difficulty in this game is authentic and it is too easy and lacks features from authentic plus in SE 4. Most notably it lacks the perpetual search enemies would start if they got made aware of you, this made the game more immersive because enemies didn't just forget you sprayed their friends brain other them 2 minutes ago and if you weren't careful you could easily have the entire base look for you. It added a lot of variety to the game and it's just gone. 

Most special enemies are gone. Older entries would have enemies calling in support like mortars to flush you out of position even if they don't know exactly where you are. Shooting officers would also delay enemy response and have them act less aggressive. This is gone, apart from snipers there are no meaningful enemies, this makes the game less dynamic and easier on all difficulties.

The range adjust doubles as a rangefinder even on authentic, letting you line up both the range marker and the wind marker essentially giving you aim assist even on authentic (because the wind marker is now 1 to 1 where the bullet will go), this makes authentic easier than it should be (especially since all the weapons got stronger too). This also goes for all the other difficulty modes ( I think they even added a new easy difficulty) making them all easier than they used to be and adding more and more help like a sort of xray mode, aim assist even on sniper elite difficulty etc.
I am not saying we should remove the easy mode but please give us back the actually immersive authentic plus mode with the search feature from SE 4, combined withe SE 5s better ballistics that would make for a great combo.

Also the invasion mode lacks a difficulty filter meaning you get put into a random game. I don't want to play with aim assist and xray mode and I am sure people who do don't want to paly without them, please let us pick a difficulty here.

Overall I want to say that is is my favorite SE but all the stuff missing from SE 4 and 3 makes this hard, I still like the new ballistics and being able to make various loadouts, but with the lack of enemy variety and the removal of the search mode it just doesn't feel as dynamic and fun anymore. I want a sniper game not a passable stealth game with aim assist snipers.

There are a lot of mid stealth games out there, there are barely any good sniping games.

I love the Sniper Elite series, but they certainly messed up this time around.

For starters, the game plays like a generic action-stealth MGS V  clone, instead of a Sniper Elite game. 

99% of all combat takes played within 50 meters, making rifles pretty useless compared to a pistol. The maps are also lacking in verticality, which is bizarre for a sniping game.
Also, in the past you could take a shot on Hard difficulty and the enemy would only be alerted. Take a few shots, and they would pinpoint your location. Only on Authentic difficulty would the enemy immediattely pinpoint your position and run towards you en masse. In Sniper Elite 5, now a single shot will immediately alert the enemy of your exact position, making sniper kills only viable from a few pre-orchastrated locations (the ones with a soundmasking generator). 

This means that apart from a few pre-orchastrated locations, you’ll be using the silenced pistol for the entire game.

They’ve also removed S-mines and Trip Mines from the game, to “streamline” the experience for new plyers. In previous Sniper Elites, you could cover your sniping location by laying those mines in doorways/stairs/etc and could make some really awesome traps that way.

Now the opportunity of trap laying is gone since you only have 2 teller mines at your disposal. What makes this even worse is that they’ve convoluted the game with all kinds of new ammo types, all of them having no de-facto advantage over the normal and subsonic ammo. They’ve also added the Shu-mine, a non-lethal mine.

However, playing non-lethal has no advantage whatsoever, since the total XP you get from that playstyle is always lower than playing lethal. 

You can also no longer replace your weapons with enemy weapons. Enemy weapons now function as disposable items; You can finish off the magazine and than they’ll disappear, Use your own weapon or item and the character will drop the enemy weapon. 

What makes matters worse is that there are a ton or rifles, smg’s and pistols in the game, but the player has only a handful of them in the load-out screen! Why create so many types of rifles, smg’s and pistols if the player can’t use them? 

The new weapon customization sounds great in theory, but the difference in stats are so little that it basically has zero use. 

What makes it worse is that they’ve removed all the different reticles you could select in previous SE games. Why would you do that? Why would you remove the Sniper out of Sniper Elite, and replace it with generic MGS/CoD stuff?

Also, the new X-ray vision looks graphically great, but all the added veins and muscles make it impossible to discern the organs and bones from it, so the X-ray vision is less conveying in damage and gore than the X-ray vision in Sniper Elite 3 and 4.

There is also an issue with enemy bodies disappearing. To unlock a new weapon, you must kill a high-ranking officer in a specific way. My tactic of preference is to pacify the officer and kill all other enemies in the area so the killing of the officer by explosion/falling objects/etc makes no sound.

However, bodies disappear very quickly after pacifying or killing them, so that officer you pacified is disappeared by the time you come back to him. You can also no longer wait to loot the body of an enemy, since the body will disappear ASAP.

What is strange is that this was an issue in Sniper Elite 3 as well, and fixed in Sniper Elite 4. Why did they revert back to a known game problem?


[b]Conclusion[/b]
If you love generic action games, buy this game for a few bucks after all the DLC’s have come out.

If you love Sniper Elite, stay clear of this entry.

Edited: Just finished the campaign and have played a bit of Axis Invasion as well. Some people are claiming you are "forced" to do Axis invasion, ie. the game mode where others can invade your game as a German sniper hunter and mess with you, because of an XP penalty if you turn it off. That is simply not true!
First of all, the game tells you that you get an XP bonus when playing with Axis Invasion turned on, so the framing of penalty is entirely a construct of the people complaining. The only thing that's true is that you do in fact earn less playing without Axis Invasion turned on, but is that actually a problem? No, it isn't, and here's why:
After having finished the main campaign [i]without Axis Invasion[/i], I'm at max level and while I didn't rush through each mission, I didn't even attempt to 100% completion either, so you get plenty of XP along the way even with the "penalty". People are just looking for a reason to be upset.

Also, Axis Invasion is super fun if you're in the mood for it. If you're not, just turn it off and know that you will not come even close to feeling that you're struggling with XP gains. I gained the final level during the final mission, so the game seems fairly well balanced around playing without Axis Invasion turned on, so the devs' claim that it is indeed a bonus is completely reasonable.

Upd: I rebought on sale and finished it. Long story short - my opinion holds.

The reason it holds is because this one doesn't know what it wants to be. Plagued with the modern devs' disease of chasing the widest audience, it tries to be Sniper Elite and Hitman trilogy at the same time. Yet without the experience or understanding of IOI, all Rebellion could do are massive, bloated (yet somehow still linear) landscapes, clearing each is gonna take hours. The maps feel like checklists - destroy AA guns, radar towers (hello Ubisoft), assassinate some targets the game doesn't care to introduce enough to make you care about. Rinse and repeat. Even though 8 levels might not sound like much, this leads to the game massively overstaying its welcome. 

A supposed star of the show here is the weapon upgrades system, which looks intriguing at a glance, but ends up being whatever. That's because all the choice the game seemingly offers gets invalidated by the design decisions behind it. Shockingly for a game called Sniper Elite, there's almost nowhere to snipe as most of the action takes place in tight corridors. So the best way to mod the sniper rifle is to take off the scope. Ammo is rare, which I wouldn't mind if all the mods that seemingly promote the spray&pray playstyle did not exist. Attaching a bayonet to a shotgun and using it like a spear is fun... what's not fun is every enemy having a fixed health pool, leading to absurd situations where said shotgun needs 2 shots point-blank for the most enemies in the second half of the game. Indeed, once you realize the magic number of 130 damage needed to one-shot most enemies, the entire arsenal gets forever split into weapons what can be modded to achieve that, and those that can't. 

Some 5 years ago I went out of my way to praise Sniper Elite 4 for how combat feels. Officers commanding their men, radiomen calling reinforcements if they are alerted... Different enemy types was a big part of that game, and 5 unfortunately does not live up to that. Officers are still there but don't really impact things anymore. Radiomen don't exist at all. I think I encountered 1 spotter in the entire game, and never had artillery called on me. And Jagers are just bullet sponges. Occassionally the game tried to spice things up by throwing in an armored car or a tank, which are hard countered by moving around them faster than the turret... eh.

If Call of Duty is too fast for you, this game is perfect. Play cadet level if you want to just relax a little and snoop around taking pop shots.
I'm 56 and this game is great for people who aren't as fast with the trigger anymore... ie, on Cadet level :-)

Sniper Elite 5 takes every excellent new gameplay refinement and addition from SE4: Italia, and makes subtle tweaks to balance out the overall formula. It's a nice touch, and just as fun to play as the previous game. It moves a bit faster than SE4, which means the game loses its sense of weight, both when running, crouching and going prone, and when firing. However, it offsets that with a more realistic approach to movement and aiming, so it's not a bad change. Maps are still MASSIVE, and can be approached any which way you like.

The game is M-A-D-E for Co-op, and it's tons of fun to play with a friend. Wife and I haven't tried Invasion Mode yet, but we will in the future. Those frustrated by the gameplay need to chill out and learn the ropes before leaving bad reviews, especially if they've never played SE4 before. It isn't perfect, and it's not a massive upgrade from SE4, but it's fun to play, and well worth the long wait time it took to come out.

Aside from a few kinks and quirks that were slightly better polished in the last game. 
Sniper Elite 5 wins me over and over again. Invasion mode was such a nice new touch and it's more fun than it is frustrating. Way better than that dam Elden Ring invasion...then again I suck at that game.

Back to the subject. If you are looking for more of the same with a tweak here and change there, then you will really enjoy SE5. It's not broke, so the devs didn't try to fix it Nor did they go all "It's the New Era, we gotta change everything!" No, they stuck to whats been working, added some things and went from there. 

Only complaints I have are these...and no, they are FAR from deal breakers. For me anyway...

1: Slow moving mechanics when interacting with ladders, vaulting or doing melee kills. It feels very stiff and clunky. Almost having you come to a full pause in mid-animation. This makes it hard to move fast and quickly in tight situations. ESPECIALLY the melee kills. Im not looking for chain melee kills, though it would be nice, but it sucks having that awkward pause in the middle of combat and you have to take hits, before taking out the next guy right in front of you.

2: Bring my ridiculous Ragdoll BACK!!! The ragdoll is still there, but they dumbed it down a bit and turned the gravity up on the weight of the enemies bodies flying.

3: Graphics isn't everything, but it can use a bit more touching up.

4: Im not sure how, but there are some things better with the X-ray attacks, but it's lacking some of the details that SE4 had. Seems like they focused really hard on making the anatomy of the human body look more real. Kinda giving it this authentic brutality look (Which is GREAT) but they kinda neglected the animations when the bullet is traveling through the brain, teeth and eyes. SE4 actually had the brain move and shake and the eyes explode. It's still there, but some how it less animated than SE4.

5: I would LOVE to see the damage I caused in the body. The SE series has always, ALWAYS had this "Mortal Kombat Gore" Thing going on, where you clearly see the teeth and brains and cranium pieces flying out and then go to the dead bodies and zoom in and see    : /   or   : l    on  what should be a mutilated face.

In closing. Love this game. It's honestly worth 60, but the devs were modest and I appreciate that. It's so much to do with the upgrades, customizing weapons (Which they took out in SE4), plenty of Multi-player and Coop fun, CROSS-PLAY, Runs SMOOOTH (2080 Super) AND....that's all I got. Remember if you see a Nazi not being very good at Nazi-ing, it's more than likely me doing a terrible job at stopping you from getting to your next objective.

After finding Sniper Elite 4 a bit of a misstep or snooze, Sniper Elite 5 is back in awesome form.

If you're new to the series, the format is large maps with a combination of stealth and shooting, similar to the new Hitman games, but without the disguises, and set in WW2.
